AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crops 1.6 Crop Protection: Weed control 1.7 General Crop Harves.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Land? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Land.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Land.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Land.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Land.

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Breeds of Livestock 2.2 Safe Handling of Animals 2.3 General Animal Health 2.4 B? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Breeds of Livestock 2.2 Safe Handling of Animals 2.3 General Animal Health 2.4 B.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Breeds of Livestock 2.2 Safe Handling of Animals 2.3 General Animal Health 2.4 B.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Breeds of Livestock 2.2 Safe Handling of Animals 2.3 General Animal Health 2.4 B.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Breeds of Livestock 2.2 Safe Handling of Animals 2.3 General Animal Health 2.4 B.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Selected Crop? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Selected Crop.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Selected Crop.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crop.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Selected Crop.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying General Crop Harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to General Crop Harvesting.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for General Crop Harvesting.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about General Crop Harvesting.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on General Crop Harvesting.

9. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Field Management Practices? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Field Management Practices.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Field Management Practices.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Field Management Practices.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Field Management Practices.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Safe Handling of Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Safe Handling of Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Safe Handling of Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Safe Handling of Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Safe Handling of Animals.

12. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Agricultural Land and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of soil and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Land Preparation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Field Management Practices and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Land.

4. C — Glucose and oxygen

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Breeds of Livestock 2.2 Safe Handling of Animals 2.3 General Animal Health 2.4 B.

6. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Selected Crop.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for General Crop Harvesting.

9. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Field Management Practices.

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Safe Handling of Animals.

12. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
